title: Tutorial: Reuse a Value With a Variable
scenario: Welcome to the guided track. A variable is a named input: the caller can change it without editing the block that uses it. Declare one input variable and expose it through an output.
constraints: Use type string and default demo-app.
Create output app_name that reads var.app_name.

focus.title: Declare the input variable
focus.todo: Add the variable metadata, its type and a default value.

hints.why: Variables are the seam between a reusable configuration and the environment that calls it. Once a value is an input, changing environments does not require editing resource code.
hints.what: Complete the variable block in variables.tf. It needs a description, a string type and the default shown in the constraints. The output already shows how the caller reads it.
hints.when: Reach for an input variable when a value changes per environment, must be supplied securely, or should be controlled by whoever calls the configuration.
hints.how: Start at the top of the `variable "app_name"` block. Add `description`, `type = string`, and `default`; keep the quotes around the default because it is a string. Run the tests and compare each failure with the constraint list.

test_manifest.title: app_name is declared with the expected type and default
the app_name output references the variable
